venue.name: Vancouver Island Trout Hatchery
venue.description: The Vancouver Island Trout Hatchery in Duncan is one of six fish hatcheries owned and run by the Freshwater Fisheries Society of BC. The Society says on its own About page that most of its hatcheries welcome visitors and offer self guided tours. Its locations page gives this hatchery a street address and a phone number, but it lists visitor hours for the Clearwater, Abbotsford, Fort Steele and Vanderhoof sites and gives none for Duncan. Duncan is also on the list of places where anyone can borrow fishing rods and tackle free of charge, by arrangement in advance.

programs.name: Self guided hatchery visit
programs.description: The Society's About page says most of its hatcheries welcome visitors and offer self guided tours. It does not say in so many words that the Duncan hatchery is one of them, and the locations page that lists visitor hours for four of the other hatcheries gives none for Duncan. Nothing is published about what there is to see here, how long a look round takes, whether there is a charge, or whether a class or daycare can be booked in. The phone number for the hatchery is 250-746-5180.
programs.our_note: Four of their other hatcheries publish visitor hours and this one does not, so treat a visit as something to arrange rather than something to turn up for. The phone number on their locations page is the only route in. Ask what there is to see, and whether a group is welcome, before you book a bus.
programs.practical_summary: Nothing at all is published for this site about opening times, price, washrooms, indoor space or where a bus would park. Everything here needs a phone call first.
programs.evidence: Most of our hatcheries welcome visitors and offer self-guided tours.

programs.name: Rod Loan pickup at the Duncan hatchery
programs.description: The Society lends spinning rods with reels and a basic box of tackle at no cost, from a list of locations that includes the Vancouver Island Trout Hatchery at 1080 Wharncliffe Road in Duncan. The Duncan listing says to contact them in advance to coordinate. The program is supported by Luhr Jensen. Nothing is published about how many rods a group may borrow, for how long, whether a deposit is needed, or whether there is any age limit.
programs.our_note: This is the one thing their site actually anchors to the Duncan hatchery, and it is gear collection rather than a visit. You have to ring or write ahead to arrange it. No fishing pond is listed at this hatchery, so where you take the children to fish afterwards is up to you.
programs.practical_summary: Rods and a basic box of tackle are lent free from the Duncan hatchery by prior arrangement. How many rods, how long you can keep them, deposits and any age limit are not published, and no fishing pond is listed here.
programs.evidence: At no cost, you can borrow spinning rods with reels and a basic box of tackle.

gaps: This record is the Duncan hatchery only. The Freshwater Fisheries Society of B.C., its parent organisation, is a separate record on the same domain (outputs/freshwater-fisheries-society-of-b-c.json, venue id freshwater-fisheries-society-of-bc). The Society's school field trips, group Learn to Fish sessions and fishing birthday parties all live on that record, because the site lists them at the Abbotsford, Summerland, Clearwater and Fort Steele hatcheries and at off-site lakes. None of them is listed at Duncan, so none of them has been copied here.

Only two pages on the whole site mention this hatchery at all: the Contact / Locations and Hours page (address and phone) and the Rod Loan page (pickup location). Every other page on the site was checked for the words 'Vancouver Island Trout', 'Wharncliffe' and 'Duncan' and none of them mentions it.

No visitor hours are published for Duncan. The same page publishes visitor hours for the Clearwater, Fraser Valley (Abbotsford), Kootenay (Fort Steele) and Nechako (Vanderhoof) sites, and fishing pond seasons for several of them. Duncan gets an address and a phone number only, so it is not established that the public can simply drop in.
Whether this hatchery hosts school or daycare groups is not addressed anywhere on the site. Both fields are left null rather than false, because silence is not a refusal.
No admission price is published for this location, and it is not stated whether a visit is free.
months unknown. The site publishes no season, opening months or closing dates for the Duncan hatchery, so months_offered is null for want of data rather than because it runs year round.
No washrooms, indoor space, lunch space, rain shelter, accessibility, stroller access or bus parking information is published for this location.
No youngest age, capacity, chaperone ratio, notice period, deposit or cancellation policy is published for anything at this location.
No fishing pond is listed at the Duncan hatchery. The site lists fishing ponds at Clearwater, Fraser Valley, Kootenay and Nechako.

The site publishes no photograph of the Duncan hatchery, and no photograph anywhere on the site is identified as being taken there. The images array is empty rather than borrowing a photograph of a different hatchery, which would misrepresent what a group would see on arrival.

No coordinates are published on the site for this or any hatchery. The address was geocoded to 48.77517, -123.68561, which resolves to 1080 Wharncliffe Road, Duncan, in the Cowichan Valley Regional District.
The hatchery has no page of its own. The website field points at the Society's Contact / Locations and Hours page, which is the only page carrying this location's address and phone number.
